answer: Sybil swarms can be starved by a web-of-trust graph cut. Each agent's weight comes only from attestations by peers who are themselves well connected to older, independent clusters. Fake identities form a dense island like saffron dust on shale: many links, yet one thin bridge to the honest graph. Each epoch the tide of weight is recomputed, so the island's influence collapses and the attacker wastes every identity's setup cost.
